title: Kentucky v. King (2011)
key_points: Holding: The exigency of preventing evidence destruction can justify warrantless entry, as long as police did not create the exigency by violating or threatening to violate the Fourth Amendment.
officer_notes: Scenario: You knock on an apartment door after smelling marijuana, announce 'Police', then hear movement consistent with evidence being destroyed.
Takeaway: Lawful knocking is OK; threatening to force entry without a basis is not. NJ courts review this closely.
